source.observed_contract: When no explicit session/conversation id is present, getOpenCodeSessionKey derives a durable-looking key from model + user/default + first user message content. That key is then used by SessionRequestGate, sessionStore, toolMemo, account/thread affinity and checkpoint recovery.
source.fresh_observation: Two unrelated OpenAI-compatible conversations with the same model, absent user identity and identical first user text derive the same key.

risk: Independent clients/tasks can alias the same durable Qwen session when they do not provide an explicit conversation id.
A new initial request can clear or replace durable state belonging to another logically independent conversation with the same first prompt.
Account/thread affinity and pending-tool safety can therefore be correlated to prompt content instead of a real conversation identity.
candidate_contract: Treat explicit x-opencode-session/x-session-id/conversation/session metadata as the only authority for durable session identity.
If the client provides no explicit identity, do not persist or reuse provider chatId/account/checkpoint state across requests under a content-derived key.
A content-derived hash may remain request-local for logs/telemetry/gating, but must not become durable conversation identity.
Do not silently invent a random durable id server-side unless it is returned to the client and then supplied back on later requests.
required_regressions: Two independent initial requests with identical first prompt and no explicit session id must not share durable state or provider chatId.
An explicit conv-A and conv-B with identical content remain isolated.
A multi-turn client that wants durable restart/continuation must supply a stable explicit conversation id.
Existing explicit OpenCode/Codex session-id paths retain sticky thread/account affinity and pending-tool protection.
limits: No hosted CI, provider traffic, real accounts, secrets, Cloudflare, Windows or production used.
